title:
The Delegation Dilemma: 
Why Agentic AI Requires Organizational Redesign
affiliations: and

detail.title:
The Delegation Dilemma: 
Why Agentic AI Requires Organizational Redesign
detail.abstract: As organizations increasingly deploy agentic artificial intelligence systems that can plan, coordinate, and execute actions, AI adoption is entering a new organizational phase. Unlike earlier AI applications that primarily supported human decision-making, agentic systems act within workflows, initiating tasks and producing consequences across systems and time. While these capabilities promise gains in speed and scalability, many organizations struggle to scale beyond pilots into stable production. Existing explanations often emphasize technical risk, overlooking the organizational conditions required to govern autonomous action. This whitepaper argues that the central challenge of agentic AI adoption is organizational rather than technical. As AI systems transition from tools to actors, organizations implicitly delegate authority without redesigning decision rights, coordination mechanisms, and accountability structures. By reframing agentic AI adoption as an organizational design problem, this paper explains why many initiatives stall after experimentation and clarifies the implications for leaders seeking to integrate autonomous systems more coherently and responsibly.

The research synthesizes recent advances in transformer-based models, hybrid deep-learning architectures, and multimodal approaches to speech emotion detection, and evaluates their suitability for real-time virtual assistant systems (Onyekwelu-Udoka et al., 2025; Hu et al., 2022). The methodology integrates a comparative literature analysis with an architectural evaluation of existing emotion-aware assistant frameworks to assess performance, scalability, and deployment feasibility (Zadeh & Alaeifard, 2023). The findings indicate that incorporating emotion-aware speech processing significantly improves user satisfaction, engagement, and task efficiency. However, persistent challenges remain, including dataset bias, computational latency, and ambiguity in emotional and contextual interpretation (Chatterjee et al., 2021; Li, 2025). The study concludes that emotion-aware speech processing is a critical component of next-generation intelligent assistants and recommends the development of unified multimodal frameworks alongside robust ethical and governance strategies to support scalable and responsible real-world adoption (Addu, 2024; Abdelaziz et al., 2025).

title: Compliance Pooling in Maritime Shipping Under Emission Intensity Caps

detail.title: Compliance Pooling in Maritime Shipping Under Emission Intensity Caps
detail.abstract: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, as an influential measure with broad coverage and significant implications for global supply chains, is currently being implemented. It targets reducing emissions in maritime transport by capping the greenhouse-gas intensity of the energy used on board, while allowing compliance pooling to facilitate this transition. A healthy pooling market is key to incentivising a transition to cleaner shipping as an opportunity to sell surplus compliance units can make investment in a cleaner ship more financially attractive. To maximise this effect the threshold and penalty need to be tuned so that the cash flows to the compliant ship are maximised. The lower the emissions threshold, the lower the supply of surplus units, the higher their price, capped by the penalty, limiting revenue to the compliant ships. But the higher the supply of surplus units, the lower their price, also limiting revenue to the compliant ships. Studying price competition and using 2024 European Union maritime emissions-reporting data, this study investigates the shipping compliance market effect on companies' costs, profits, and penalties. It provides prescriptive insights for regulators on implementing emission-reduction policy and adopting market-based tools under dynamic market conditions.

title: Between Clicks and Crowds: Operational Spillovers from Digital Engagement to Offline Care Quality
affiliations: University of Houston - C.T. Bauer College of Business, Guangdong University of Technology and City University of Hong Kong (CityU), affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Between Clicks and Crowds: Operational Spillovers from Digital Engagement to Offline Care Quality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors are not aware of any conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors have no funders to report.

detail.abstract: At scale, physician-led online health consultation communities (OHCs) are increasingly becoming a front entrance to healthcare delivery. By enabling patient-centric physician selection under noisy reputation signals and patient bias, OHCs are reshaping healthcare demand and inducing new matching dynamics that can inadvertently spill over into offline inpatient operations. These platforms can disrupt capacity management and clinical quality as patient-driven self-routing reallocates demand across physicians in ways uncoordinated with offline clinical triage, challenges that the traditional healthcare operations were not designed, nor sufficiently prepared, to respond to. Though OHCs can improve patient access by extending physicians’ reach beyond physical boundaries, their cross-channel operational externalities on offline healthcare operations and inpatient quality remain unclear. We assemble a 28-month, operation-level panel dataset combining 166,076 inpatient episodes and online activity data of 484 physicians across four leading OHCs to examine our research questions. We find that OHC participation significantly worsens clinical outcomes indicating a negative operational externality, as evidenced by an increase in the length of hospital stay, deterioration in discharge status, and an elevation in readmission risk. We theorize and validate the critical role played by patient-doctor mismatch (PDM), defined as the severity-skill misalignment in how patients get treated by physicians, as a key operational mechanism. Mediation analyses show that physicians’ OHC participation elevates their inpatient volume and congestion, which in turn increases PDM and degrades quality, revealing a crowding-out pathway. Consistent with noisy quality signals induced on digital platforms, we find some evidence for a reputation-halo bias, whereby patients conflate popularity with clinical skill. We further identify heterogeneity: the adverse effects are mitigated among patients with an agricultural occupation who tend to rely on conventional provider-driven triage, and among female physicians whose online reputation signals might be less inflated by societal perceptions. We introduce PDM as an operational construct linking physicians’ digital engagement to offline quality degradation, thereby revealing how patient-centric platforms can disrupt operations and care quality in traditional offline healthcare settings.

title: From Guilds to Margins: A Historical-Economic Reclassification Study of the Vankar Community in India

detail.title: From Guilds to Margins: A Historical-Economic Reclassification Study of the Vankar Community in India
detail.abstract: This paper examines the historical-economic trajectory of the Vankar community through archaeological, epigraphic, trade, colonial economic, and census records. It argues that the contemporary classification of the community as a Scheduled Caste is not rooted in ritualpurity based social exclusion, but rather in a long process of economic displacement, deindustrialization, and administrative reclassification. Using evidence from Indus Valley archaeology (Lothal), Gupta-period inscriptions (Mandasor), Mughal-era trade systems, colonial tariff policy, famine records, and the 1931 Census of India, the study proposes that occupational collapse and loss of economic autonomy—rather than religious untouchability—were the primary drivers of social downgrading. The paper contributes to caste studies by introducing an economic-deindustrialization model of caste mobility and reclassification.

title: Market Effects on Liner Shipping Alliances and Cooperation Strategies
affiliations: , The University of Sydney, The University of Sydney and The University of Sydney Business School

detail.title: Market Effects on Liner Shipping Alliances and Cooperation Strategies
detail.abstract: Container shipping lines choose cooperation when it improves their profitability. The highly cyclical nature of demand for container shipping affects the profit of container shipping lines, and correspondingly, influences their cooperation strategies. Additionally, the profit of shipping lines depends on the fees they pay to ports and terminal operators, which, in turn, are influenced by the level of competition between terminal operators. Therefore, the motivation for shipping lines to ally is affected by the bargaining power they gain over customers, ports, and terminal operators. This research studies the combined effect of market demand and port competition on shipping line cooperation. An evolutionary game theory model is developed to study the dynamics of cooperation among shipping lines. Additionally, container ports and terminal operators compete to attract shipping lines by reducing their container handling fees while maintaining profitability. It is demonstrated that the cooperation among liner companies prevails as market demand increases relative to supply. Port and terminal operators' market power intensifies this effect by increasing fee savings. With high enough demand, cooperation dominates in the market in the form of vessel-sharing agreements or alliances. However, their evolutionary equilibrium cooperation depends on market shares, freight rate, and charter rate. Our computational results suggest that increasing demand fluctuations intensify cooperation, while increasing shipping capacity relative to demand weakens it.

detail.abstract: This paper applies network analysis to examine the impact of non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) and financial market stress on contagion risk within the interbank network. Using network-based simulations on euro area banks’ supervisory data, we find that banks’ strong capital and liquidity buffers significantly reduce contagion through interbank exposures: base-line scenarios show only modest capital losses and no cascading defaults. In contrast, stress originating from NBFIs under heightened market volatility markedly amplifies systemic risk. These findings highlight NBFIs and market volatility as key amplifiers of financial stress in the euro area. Our findings call for integrating contagion models into system-wide stress testing and designing macroprudential policies that encompass the entire financial ecosystem. Such policies should account for amplification risks from banks’ NBFI exposures when calibrating buffers and identifying systemic institutions.

The paper reframes GenAI governance as a strategic decision architecture problem and develops a conceptual model that explains how organizations can embed GenAI into their decision systems to convert adoption into sustained strategic decision value.

title: Data Confidence as a Strategic Capability: Turning Insights into Influence

detail.title: Data Confidence as a Strategic Capability: Turning Insights into Influence
detail.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to introduce data confidence as a strategic capability that enables executives to transform analytical insights into decision influence. While organizations increasingly invest in analytics and data governance, many struggle to embed data into strategic decision-making. This paper argues that the missing link is not analytical sophistication, but confidence in data as a credible, interpretable, and actionable input for strategy. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual and integrative approach, synthesizing insights from strategy, knowledge management, analytics capability, and decision-making literatures to develop data confidence as a strategic capability. Rather than employing empirical testing, the study draws on established theoretical and managerial research to identify the conditions under which data-based insights translate into strategic influence. The approach emphasizes managerial relevance and executive decision contexts, focusing on how trust, interpretability, governance structures, and organizational decision routines jointly shape confidence in data. By integrating these streams, the paper develops a conceptual framework that explains how data confidence enables executives to act on insights in strategic settings. Findings This paper advances three interrelated conceptual findings that explain why data-driven insights often fail to influence strategic decision-making and how data confidence operates as a strategic capability that enables insight to translate into influence. The first finding is that the strategic influence of data is determined less by data availability or analytical sophistication than by the degree of confidence decision-makers place in data-based insights. While organizations increasingly develop advanced analytics capabilities, these capabilities do not automatically shape strategic action. Data influences strategy only when executives perceive it as credible, interpretable, and relevant to their decision context. In the absence of such confidence, data remains informational rather than influential, regardless of its technical quality. The second finding is that data confidence is best understood as a multi-dimensional organizational capability rather than a single attribute of data or technology. Conceptually, data confidence comprises cognitive confidence, reflecting executives’ ability to interpret and make sense of data; relational confidence, reflecting trust in data sources and analytical processes; and structural confidence, reflecting governance mechanisms and decision routines that legitimize data use. These dimensions interact to shape whether insights are accepted, debated, or acted upon in strategic forums. Weaknesses in any one dimension can undermine overall confidence, even when analytical outputs are technically sound. The third finding is that data confidence functions as the critical mechanism through which insights are translated into influence within strategic decision processes. When confidence is high, executives are more likely to sponsor data-based arguments, defend them in deliberations, and integrate them into strategic choices. When confidence is low, insights are more easily overridden by intuition, experience, or organizational politics. From this perspective, data confidence represents a distinct strategic capability that shapes not only decision quality but also the distribution of influence within strategic conversations. Originality/value This paper makes a novel contribution by introducing data confidence as a distinct strategic capability that explains why data-driven insights often fail to influence executive decisionmaking. While prior research has emphasized data quality, analytics capability, or governance maturity, this paper shifts attention to the behavioral and organizational conditions under which data becomes influential in strategic contexts. By integrating insights from strategy, knowledge management, and decision-making literature, the paper reframes analytics not as a technical asset but as a source of strategic influence mediated by confidence. The value of the paper lies in offering executives a practical lens for diagnosing why analytics investments underperform and for designing confidence-building mechanisms that enable insights to shape strategic outcomes.

Empirical evaluations conducted in simulated supply chain environments demonstrate significant improvements in forecast accuracy, inventory turnover, and logistics agility compared to traditional Al approaches. The proposed framework offers a scalable, interpretable, and practically deployable architecture for transforming supply chain decision-making, contributing to the development of intelligent, resilient, and sustainable supply chain ecosystems.

title: Empire of Patents- Corporate Research Trajectories and the Future Geography of Innovation

detail.title: Empire of Patents- Corporate Research Trajectories and the Future Geography of Innovation
detail.abstract: This study investigates the evolution of global technological power through a detailed analysis of U.S. patent registrations by leading multinational corporations between 2021 and 2024. Leveraging USPTO datasets and applying frameworks from innovation economics, intellectual property theory, and geopolitical technology studies, the paper identifies structural patterns in research specialization, emerging scientific frontiers, and corporate–state innovation alignments. The findings indicate that firms such as Samsung, TSMC, LG, Apple, Qualcomm, Huawei, IBM, Alphabet, Sony, Toyota, Intel, Microsoft, and Amazon are not only competing in traditional sectors like semiconductors, displays, and communications, but are also constructing new technological architectures in AI hardware, quantum systems, advanced batteries, robotics, photonics, and autonomous mobility. Data reveal a shift from quantity-driven to specialization-driven patent strategies, with companies leveraging proprietary ecosystems to secure technological sovereignty. Drawing historical parallels with ancient knowledge monopolies, the study underscores how intellectual control continues to shape economic and political power. It concludes by forecasting the rise of multi-domain technological blocs, dominated by vertically integrated firms, signaling a transition toward a global order defined by innovation asymmetry and patent-driven geopolitical influence.

title: Cryptographic Lineages and the Genesis of Bitcoin
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Cryptographic Lineages and the Genesis of Bitcoin
detail.abstract: This research paper reconstructs the historical, technical, and sociopolitical foundations of Bitcoin by examining the contributions of Adam Back, Hal Finney, Satoshi Nakamoto, and the cypherpunk movement that shaped early digital cash concepts. Drawing on primary sources, cryptographic literature, archived mailing-list communications, and interdisciplinary historical analogies, the study situates the development of Hashcash (1997) and Finney’s reusable proof-of-work (2004) within the broader evolution of cryptographic trust mechanisms, tracing their lineage back to ancient systems of authentication, secrecy, and economic signaling. By analyzing Adam Back’s academic formation—including A-levels in mathematics, physics, economics, and his 1995 PhD in distributed systems at the University of Exeter—alongside his work on applied cryptography, credlib e-cash libraries, and non-interactive forward secrecy, the paper demonstrates how these innovations directly influenced Bitcoin’s proof-of-work architecture. The study incorporates Hal Finney’s role as the first recipient of a Bitcoin transaction, his involvement in early cryptographic networks, and forensic insights such as the Patoshi Pattern, while contextualizing Satoshi Nakamoto’s 2011 disappearance and the subsequent transition of leadership to Gavin Andresen. Drawing historical parallels—from Mesopotamian accounting tokens to Roman ciphers and Renaissance secrecy practices—the research highlights recurring civilizational patterns in which cryptographic systems emerge during periods of institutional fragility and technological transformation. It concludes that Bitcoin represents the culmination of decades of scientific innovation and centuries of human experimentation with trust, illustrating how principles of costly signaling, privacy, and decentralized authority persist in modern digital monetary systems.

title: Decoding Pakistan’s Multi-Front War Preparations: A Hybrid Analysis of Saturation Warfare.
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Decoding Pakistan’s Multi-Front War Preparations: A Hybrid Analysis of Saturation Warfare.
detail.abstract: This paper examines Pakistan’s evolving strategy to conduct multi-front hybrid warfare against India, employing saturation attacks, ideological mobilization, maritime encirclement, and foreign-supported defense partnerships. Using intelligence-style field analysis, historical warfare patterns, open-source defense transfer data, and trends in modern military technology, the study argues that Pakistan is increasingly adopting Hamas-style drone and rocket saturation tactics to deplete India’s Air Defence System (ADS) resources. The research highlights the roles of Turkey, the United States, Bangladesh, Maldives, Sri Lanka, and Nepal in forming indirect or direct alignments that enhance Pakistan’s strategic options, with Turkey supplying advanced drones, missile systems, and AI-enabled autonomous warfare technologies. The study further examines transnational radicalization networks, including those led by Ghulam Sheikh in Nepal, and internal ideological mobilization within India as a psychological front. Grounded in Kautilya’s Mandala Theory, medieval multi-vector invasions, and early Islamic mobilization strategies, the paper concludes that future conflicts will differ fundamentally from conventional South Asian wars, characterized by autonomous swarm operations, maritime flanking, and societal disruption. This hybrid academic–intelligence assessment provides policymakers with insights into India’s emerging security environment.

title: A Public Law Perspective to Cryptocurrency and Economic Crimes in Nigeria
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Public Law Perspective to Cryptocurrency and Economic Crimes in Nigeria
detail.abstract: Cryptocurrency has rapidly emerged as both a transformative financial technology and a facilitator of economic crimes worldwide. In Nigeria, adoption levels are among the highest globally, driven by factors such as inflation, currency instability, and financial exclusion, yet accompanied by a rise in incidents of fraud, money laundering, and related offenses. Regulatory bodies, such as the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), have sought to respond. However, early reliance on ad hoc circulars and general financial statutes has led to regulatory overlaps, enforcement inconsistencies, and constitutional concerns. The recent passage of the Investment and Securities Act (ISA) 2025 provides a more coherent legal foundation by expressly classifying virtual assets as securities and granting the SEC supervisory powers over these assets. Nevertheless, gaps remain in enforcement coordination, constitutional safeguards, and victim protection. This research, adopting a doctrinal and comparative methodology, examines Nigeria's evolving framework for addressing crypto-related economic crimes through the lens of public law. It analyses statutes, regulatory guidelines, and case law, while drawing lessons from international frameworks such as the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recommendations. The study argues for further reforms to harmonise Nigeria's approach, safeguard rights, and strengthen institutional coherence, thereby aligning with global best practices while protecting the financial system and citizens from the risks of crypto-enabled economic crimes.

title: Deep Learning of Derivatives Pricing Functions in Jump-Diffusion Models
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - Department of Systems Engineering & Engineering Management, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - Department of Systems Engineering & Engineering Management and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Deep Learning of Derivatives Pricing Functions in Jump-Diffusion Models
detail.abstract: We study the pricing of financial derivatives as functions of time, state variables, and parameters in the model and contract. Traditional computational methods evaluate the derivative price only for fixed parameters, which becomes prohibitively time-consuming when a large number of valuations are required. To enhance computational efficiency, we approximate the derivative pricing function by deep neural networks (DNNs), allowing some components of the model to vary as time-dependent functions. We train the DNN via a loss function derived from the martingale property of the discounted derivative price process, providing a unified training framework for different types of derivatives. For European options under jump-diffusion models, we theoretically prove that DNNs can overcome the curse of dimensionality in learning the pricing function. Numerical experiments on European, path-dependent, and Bermudan options confirm the effectiveness of our approach.

title: From Delhi to Karachi to Beijing: Rahul Gandhi, Infrastructure Finance, and Patterns of Strategic Influence
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Delhi to Karachi to Beijing: Rahul Gandhi, Infrastructure Finance, and Patterns of Strategic Influence
detail.abstract:
This investigative research paper examines the convergence of transnational capital flows, strategic infrastructure ownership, and political symbolism through a documented case involving a senior global investment executive, his institutional affiliations, and historically sensitive geopolitical contexts. Grounded in publicly available court filings, regulatory disclosures, investigative journalism, and corporate records, the study traces the institutional genealogy linking Soros Economic Development Fund, Aspada Investment Company, Lightrock, and The Abraaj Group, with particular attention to the attempted 2016 sale of Pakistanʼs largest electricity utility, K-Electric, to a Chinese state owned enterprise for USD 1.77 billion. Rather than positing a conspiracy, this paper adopts a systems-level analytical framework to examine how critical infrastructure—particularly energy grids and health-technology platforms—serves as nodes of latent power within complex adaptive systems. Integrating insights from energy security, epidemiology, and network theory, the study demonstrates how control over such systems can influence economic stability, public health outcomes, and political legitimacy without direct coercion. Historical analogies, including Roman provincial infrastructure, Mauryan economic governance as outlined in the Arthashastra, and Hellenistic service-based patronage, illustrate recurring structural patterns across civilizations.

The analysis further explores the role of political symbolism and elite networks in high-friction geopolitical contexts, drawing on signaling theory and deterrence literature. The paper concludes that modern democratic states face structural vulnerabilities not from isolated actors, but from the convergence of capital, infrastructure, and perception, which often outpaces regulatory oversight. It argues that enhanced transparency, historical literacy, and systems-aware governance are essential to safeguarding national interests in an era where power increasingly operates through contracts rather than conquest.

title: Side-Channel Compliance
affiliations: University of Iowa - College of Law

detail.title: Side-Channel Compliance
detail.abstract:
When a corporation commits a crime, prosecutors, judges, and managers must decide how to prevent the offense from recurring. The familiar approach is to implement what this article calls "targeted compliance," i.e. policies and procedures that directly address whatever institutional vulnerability allowed the crime to occur. Targeted compliance has, at best, a mixed track record. 

This Article introduces, theorizes, and tests a different approach--"side-channel compliance." Rather than target the institutional source of crime directly, side-channel compliance works by raising the general salience of a possibly unrelated prosocial value (like ecological stewardship, gender equality, or fair trade) within the workplace and the firm's corporate identity. Drawing on business ethics, marketing science, and organizational psychology, the Article offers multiple theoretical frameworks to motivate side-channel compliance. It then makes the empirical case that side-channel compliance works using an original, hand-collected dataset of 1,673 measurements of sociality for corporate criminals over a ten-year span. The data show that worse scores predict future criminality. Side-channel compliance offers exciting new possibilities for how legal authorities and business managers approach compliance, both before and after crime occurs.

Purpose
This research highlights the importance of the well-being of police professionals, as they are responsible for ensuring public safety.

Using structural equation modeling and multigroup analysis on a sample of 180 public police officers, the study examines the mediating role of cynicism between role conflict and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) and hostile behaviors. detail.abstract: Various programs aimed at improving energy efficiency and sustainability, which are actively implemented around the world at regional, national and local levels, are one of the powerful means for solving the problem of greenhouse gas emissions. In our study, we propose an approach to improve the efficiency, pace and scope of such targeted programs by establishing closer mutually beneficial interaction between the centers (initiators) of these programs and their participants (project implementers) at all stages of program formation and implementation. We examined the advantages of the proposed approach based on a formalized simulation model and an algorithm that implements procedures for optimal coordination and balancing of joint efforts of centers, participants, implementers, and investors, allowing them to test different strategies using sequential iterative project selection procedures. The model is built on the basis of theoretical provisions of Bellman’s principle of optimality, enabling to formalize the gradual change of the selection procedure by a set of state variables, limited by technical, economic, energy, etc. conditions of technological processes of projects. This allowed us to reduce the process of solving the formulated multidimensional optimization problem of dynamic programming to the sequential solution of simpler one-dimensional problems. To numerically assess the capabilities of the approach, we used the time value of money discounting technique, comparing the performance of the investments required to implement the projects. This made it possible to develop and analyze the results of two boundary scenarios of program implementation, as well as to identify and quantify the effect of “redistribution” (reallocation) of saved resources (energy, economic, financial) between projects, to which researchers have not paid much attention. The impact of this effect is quite large. So, in our example of improving the efficiency of program projects from 0.7 to 0.8, it is possible to achieve an increase in energy savings up to 1.7 times.

detail.abstract:
Purpose
Public police professionals must deal with complex and disruptive social, political and organizational environments. This fact highlights the key role that leadership can play in effectively managing their work, while also ensuring their well-being. The aim of this research is to analyze the influence of laissez-faire versus authentic leadership on the work engagement of police professionals, considering the mediating role of emotional exhaustion and the moderating role of resilience and self-efficacy.

Design/methodology/approach
Structural equation modeling and hierarchical multiple regression analysis were used in a sample of 184 public police professionals.

Findings
The results show that emotional exhaustion partially mediates the relationship between authentic leadership and work engagement, and fully mediates the relationship between laissez-faire leadership and work engagement. Moreover, resilience moderates the relationships between authentic leadership, emotional exhaustion and work engagement; and self-efficacy moderates the relationships between laissez-faire leadership and emotional exhaustion and between laissez-faire leadership and work engagement.

Originality/value
This study highlights that constructive leadership is an important driver of positive experiences at work; it is necessary to change from passive to constructive leadership; and it is important for the combination of psychological resources and positive leadership to improve police professionals’ well-being.

detail.abstract:
Education systems compensate teachers as instructional staff. A portion of paid instructional time is routinely devoted to stabilizing classroom conditions before instruction can proceed. This stabilization work includes behavioral regulation, emotional containment, classroom recovery, and restoration of baseline operability. It occurs within salaried roles and does not generate a separate budget signal.

This paper distinguishes instructional time from stabilization time. Sustained diversion of labor toward stabilization reduces effective instructional yield without altering formal staffing inputs. Because accounting systems track headcount and expenditure rather than internal time allocation, divergence between funded capacity and realized instructional output remains largely unmeasured.

The analysis traces how absorbed stabilization labor produces secondary organizational effects, including increased absenteeism, expanded substitute utilization, administrative load growth, remediation layering, and workforce attrition. Attrition converts previously absorbed labor demand into explicit replacement cost but does not eliminate the underlying stabilization requirement. Teacher time functions as compensatory institutional infrastructure servicing accumulated readiness debt.

The paper is diagnostic. It does not prescribe reform. It clarifies how rising expenditure can coexist with constrained instructional capacity and why institutions frequently respond to downstream indicators rather than upstream allocation shifts.

detail.abstract: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita remains the dominant metric for cross-country comparisons of economic performance, despite extensive evidence that it inadequately reflects individuals lived economic conditions. By construction, GDP per capita captures aggregate output but obscures how economic gains are transmitted to households, how income is distributed, and how far earnings translate into real purchasing power across different price environments. This paper addresses this persistent measurement gap by introducing the Balanced Prosperity Index (BPI), a pre-specified and economically grounded composite indicator designed to approximate real and inclusive material prosperity. The BPI conceptualizes prosperity as the interaction of three non-substitutable dimensions: national productive capacity, proxied by GDP per capita adjusted for purchasing power parity; typical household welfare, captured through cost-of-living-adjusted median (or representative) income; and inclusiveness of economic outcomes, measured by the inverse of the Gini coefficient. The contribution of the paper is strictly measurement oriented. It does not seek to replace GDP, explain subjective well-being, or resolve normative debates on inequality, but rather to improve how economic performance is summarized when the analytical objective is to approximate typical material living standards. Methodologically, the index is constructed following established best practices for composite indicators, including transparent normalization, explicitly declared weighting schemes, alternative aggregation structures, and pre-specified robustness checks. The empirical implementation is designed to rely on harmonized international data and to be evaluated through robustness and sensitivity analysis and comparison with external welfare-related proxies, including selected poverty-related indicators, where available. By linking output, income distribution, and purchasing power within a single transparent framework, the BPI provides a replication-friendly tool for comparative economic analysis and policy-relevant assessment of inclusive prosperity.

Purpose
This study analyzes the mediating effect of emotional exhaustion between certain job demands (workload, role conflict, and influence at work) and employees' work attitudes (affective commitment and turnover intention) in public healthcare. Design/methodology/approach
A total of 512 healthcare professionals participated in the study. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and a hierarchical multiple regression analysis.

Findings
The results show that emotional exhaustion fully mediates the relationship between job demands (workload and role conflict) and work attitudes (affective commitment and turnover intention). Moreover, the possibilities for development and degree of freedom at work moderate the relationship between role conflict and emotional exhaustion.

Strategies should be designed to prevent employees from becoming emotionally exhausted and lead them to feel more motivated, which results in a more effective public healthcare service.

Originality/value
This study stresses the importance of analyzing the role of emotional exhaustion in the public healthcare context. It demonstrates the mediating role of this variable between several antecedents and consequences, and it analyzes whether other relevant variables can moderate the negative effects of emotional exhaustion.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a series of expert comments on the Canadian Competition Bureau's Draft Enforcement Guidelines on Anti-competitive Conduct and Agreements. It engages with the draft on a thematic, rather than line-by-line, basis, focusing on foundational questions raised by the recent reforms to the Competition Act and their implications for enforcement guidance. The paper examines the role of guidelines in a period of transition, the relationship between the draft Guidelines and the Competition Act, and the consequences of expanded private access to competition law enforcement. It also addresses substantive issues including market power thresholds, theories of harm, coordinated effects, remedies, excessive and unfair pricing, and environmental agreements. The analysis highlights both innovative aspects of the draft and areas where greater clarity, differentiation, or statutory anchoring may be required, with the aim of contributing constructively to the Bureau's consultation process and to broader debates on the future direction of Canadian competition law.

title: Removal of Emerging Contaminants from Water Using Advanced Oxidation Processes (AOPs)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Removal of Emerging Contaminants from Water Using Advanced Oxidation Processes (AOPs)
detail.abstract: The increasing detection of emerging contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, endocrine-disrupting compounds, perand polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and personal care products in surface water, groundwater, and drinking water systems has raised significant environmental and public health concerns worldwide. Conventional water and wastewater treatment processes are often ineffective at fully removing these persistent and bioactive compounds, necessitating the development of more advanced remediation strategies. This study presents a systematic evaluation and synthesis of recent advances in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), focusing on reaction mechanisms, operational configurations, and performance trends reported in contemporary research. Key AOPs examined include ozonation-based systems, UV-driven processes, Fenton and photo-Fenton reactions, photocatalysis, and sulfate radical-based technologies. The analysis indicates that AOPs demonstrate high degradation efficiencies for a broad range of emerging contaminants, although performance varies significantly depending on water matrix composition, oxidant selection, and operational conditions. Notable trade-offs are identified between contaminant removal efficiency, energy consumption, chemical requirements, and the formation of potentially harmful transformation byproducts. Overall, the review highlights that while AOPs show strong potential for large-scale implementation, challenges related to cost, process optimization, and by-product control remain critical barriers. Future research should prioritize hybrid treatment systems, validation under real-water conditions, comprehensive toxicity assessment of oxidation products, and post-deployment monitoring frameworks to enhance the sustainability and regulatory acceptance of AOP-based water treatment solutions.

detail.title: Drones over the Horizon: Prospects and Constraints for a Domestic Capability
detail.abstract: This study investigates the prospects and constraints of establishing a sovereign drone capability in the Philippines as both a technological and strategic imperative. It proposes a Drone Capability Framework that conceptualizes feasibility across four interdependent dimensions: technical, organizational, legal, and sovereign. The findings reveal that the Philippines demonstrates a comparative advantage in software sovereignty, through open-source flight systems, data analytics, and cybersecurity development, yet remains constrained by hardware dependencies, particularly in semiconductors, sensors, and batteries. Organizationally, fragmented R&D efforts across major services of the Armed Forces inhibit coordination, underscoring the need for an institutionalized Drone Systems Integration Office to consolidate capability development. Regulatory analysis shows that existing policies emphasize airspace operations but lack manufacturing and certification standards, suggesting a dual-tier governance model integrating civilian and defense oversight. The study recommends that sovereignty in drone capability must be understood as a process of technological autonomy, anchored on human capital, ethical design, and local innovation, rather than complete self-sufficiency. This framework advances the discourse on self-reliant defense posture and contributes to emerging scholarship on dual-use technologies and security-industrial development in small and middle-power states.

detail.abstract: This article explores how the digital solidarity economy (DSE) framework can be applied to the governance of false information by analysing the case of Cofacts, a community-led fact-checking platform in Taiwan. Based on the theoretical framework of DSE, this article analyses Cofacts' governance, economic model, knowledge and technology policies, and social responsibilities. Through systematic comparison with the other major fact-checking models in Taiwan, the study demonstrates Cofacts' distinct strengths in participatory openness, decentralised editorial processes, and civic-aligned values. These comparative advantages position Cofacts as a locally grounded, DSE-aligned alternative to commercial-and expert-centric approaches. Yet, the analysis also reveals critical tensions, including sustainability, scale, inclusiveness, and effectiveness. Cofacts' responses, such as platform integration for reach and ongoing community-building empowerment, offer valuable insights into how DSE values may be adapted under real-world constraints. By introducing false information governance as a new application domain for DSE, this article contributes both theoretically and empirically to the ongoing discussions.

detail.title: Beyond Uptime: Actionable Performance Metrics for EV Charging Site Operators
detail.abstract: The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) depends heavily on the reliability of charging infrastructure, yet approximately 1 in 5 drivers report being unable to charge during station visits due to inoperable equipment. While regulatory efforts such as the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program have established uptime requirements, these metrics are often simplistic, delayed, and fail to provide the diagnostic granularity needed by Charging Site Operators (CSOs). Despite their pivotal role in maintaining and improving site performance, CSOs have been largely overlooked by existing reporting standards. In this paper, we propose a suite of readily computable, actionable performance metrics---Fault Time, Fault-Reason Time, and Unreachable Time---that decompose charger behavior into operationally meaningful states. Unlike NEVI uptime, these metrics are defined over configurable periods and distinguish between hardware malfunctions and network connectivity issues. We demonstrate the computation of these metrics using \evsee{}, our open-source tool that derives performance data from existing infrastructure without requiring hardware modifications. A case study involving 98 chargers at Stanford University spanning 2018--2024 demonstrates that these metrics reveal a persistent baseline of dysfunctional chargers and high-frequency network instability that remain hidden in standard annual reporting, as well as specific fault reasons that site operator can use to address on-site performance issues.

detail.abstract: The multi-trillion defined contribution retirement and investment management industries are about to be transformed. There has been a significant push by the private equity industry and traditional asset management firms to now include private equity (“PE”) investments, ultimately potentially including private equity, venture capital, real estate, private credit and possibly crypto, in retail client retirement accounts. These accounts are managed by individuals either in their 401K plans or by their companies in pooled defined contribution plans managed by external investment managers. Should mom include private investments in her 401K? Should my son? Should I? Do we understand these investments? We address the rationale currently proffered by PE firms to “democratize” access to PE investments for retail investors, which could revolutionize both the PE and large investment management firms, such as Vanguard, Black Rock, Fidelity, among others. We examine the rationales for these investments. It is important to note that we are not critiquing PE investments per se. The focus here is the execution of the investment strategy suggested for individual investors. We posit an alternative to accomplish access to this asset class at a lower cost without the burden of illiquidity. This execution mechanism appears superior to direct investments in private PE funds and clearly potentially disruptive to the PE and investment management industries.

title: A New Operational Primitive for Automated Intersections

detail.abstract: Existing intersection control approaches for automated vehicles (AVs) span a wide spectrum: traditional phase-based signal control does not fully leverage the opportunities enabled by AV controllability, whereas individual-vehicle reservation systems operate at a fine granularity but face substantial computational and scalability challenges. Yet neither paradigm achieves a practical balance between flexibility and tractability. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a new operational primitive for automated intersections, called service modes, defined as a cyclic, conflict-free vehicle passage pattern through an intersection. Service modes are constructed using a capacityoriented principle that aligns their cycle-average service rates with the geometry-induced capacity frontier. Once a diverse and representative service mode library is available, intersection operation reduces to selecting among these modes according to observed traffic conditions. In this way, service modes cast automated intersection control into a coherent and structured framework with provable stability guarantees. A case study demonstrates expanded achievable capacity and improved delay performance relative to human-driven-vehicle (HDV) settings. By combining the structural simplicity of signal-based control with the flexibility afforded by fine-grained AV motion, service modes provide an interpretable, practical, and computationally efficient foundation for automated intersection management.

title: Multi-Scale Traffic Simulation for Evaluating Large-Scale Automated Vehicle Deployment
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, SaferDrive AI, Ann Arbor and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title: Multi-Scale Traffic Simulation for Evaluating Large-Scale Automated Vehicle Deployment
detail.abstract: Traffic simulation provides a controllable, efficient, and cost-effective tool for testing and evaluating the development of automated vehicles (AVs). While many previous studies have focused on developing high-fidelity microscopic simulations to assess AV safety performance, such simulations are typically limited in scale due to their substantial computational cost. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a co-simulation framework for evaluating large-scale AV deployments. The framework adopts a multi-scale approach, in which road segments surrounding AVs are modeled using microscopic simulation, while other segments are represented through mesoscopic simulation. The primary challenge of this approach lies in coupling simulations at different scales. To address this challenge, we identify key consistency issues that must be resolved, including interior consistency and boundary consistency, and propose corresponding solutions. In particular, we introduce a novel method that solves a local Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) model to handle the spatial consistency problem. This paper also provides a computational cost analysis of the proposed co-simulation framework based on the stationary traffic condition. The framework is implemented in the SUMO environment and tested under both simple and network-level scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly reduce computational cost without compromising modeling accuracy.

detail.title: How Religious Values Shape Organizational Citizenship Behavior
detail.abstract: This paper shows that the internalization of transcendent values that prioritize collective welfare over self-interest predicts organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) through a valuecongruence mechanism. Using survey data from 181 employees across Indian organizations, we find that highly religious employees exhibit significantly greater citizenship behaviors (β = 0.34, 95% CI [0.27, 0.41], p < 0.001), an effect that persists after controlling for job satisfaction and that operates independently of organizational climate. Contrary to theoretical expectations derived from person-environment fit theory, organizational climate does not moderate the religiosity-OCB relationship (β interaction = 0.05, p = 0.29), suggesting that religious values function as portable moral resources that shape workplace behavior regardless of contextual support. These findings challenge the prevailing emphasis on situational antecedents of OCB and identify religiosity as an individual-level driver that merits greater attention in organizational behavior research. For managers, the results imply that religiosity serves as a stable predictor of discretionary effort-one that organizational interventions neither easily amplify nor suppress.

Drawing on phenomenology, neurobiology, and systems theory, it identifies the structural conditions under which observation becomes creative rather than merely reflective, and offers falsifiable predictions to distinguish durable transformation from narrative coherence alone. detail.abstract: Can machines make humans unable to tell the difference between reality and fiction? Even better, will AI be able to make our dreams appear to come true by turning fantasies into reality? In this paper, a business-oriented framework about artificial environments dubbed the Artificial Environment Matrix, or the Augmented Reality-Mixed Reality-Digital Reality-Virtual Reality framework, is introduced to provide a theoretical foundation to how each relate. The Artificial Environment Matrix sharpens the influential AR-VR framework by applying the two fundamental dimensions of AI adoption; the effortlessness of AI adoption with the augmentation-automation continuum and the objective of AI adoption with the parity-superiority continuum. By subcategorizing both augmentation and replacement of reality by the goals of developing such virtual environments, this framework is intended to help business managers and the public communicate the types of virtual environments in a more consistent manner than allowed by previously proposed frameworks. Along the way, the definition of reality is also sharpened by focusing on what is being experienced or created, using the concept of world foundation rules. Building from this foundation, a third dimension, the user-developer perspectives of AI adoption, or the subjective-objective continuum, is added to introduce the Expanded Artificial Environment Matrix, or the Artificial Environment Cube. Combined with the AI Adoption Turing Test, which tests for the indistinguishability of services rendered by AI against human-serviced jobs, eight specialized frameworks related to the advancement of artificial environments are proposed.

title: Enhancing Student Reflection in Values Education through AI- Powered Tools: A Penzu-based Study in Support of the MATATAG Curriculum

detail.title: Enhancing Student Reflection in Values Education through AI- Powered Tools: A Penzu-based Study in Support of the MATATAG Curriculum
detail.abstract:
This study investigates how integrating Penzu, an AI-powered digital journaling platform, into the Values Education curriculum enhances the depth and quality of student reflections among Grade 7 learners at Carmona National High School. Grounded in the MATATAG Curriculum, the research addresses the challenges of student disengagement and superficial reflections by providing a secure, accessible, and interactive digital space that fosters ethical development, personal insight, and mindful use of technology. The study aims to guide educators in leveraging AI tools to promote authentic reflection and holistic values formation in the digital age.

Using a mixed methods research design, the study combined quantitative and qualitative approaches to evaluate the impact of Penzu on students’ reflective practices. Sixty purposively selected students from six sections participated in the study. Data were collected through structured journaling prompts embedded in Penzu, a reflective thinking questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews with selected participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and correlation analysis, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. The integration of these methods provided a comprehensive understanding of how digital journaling enhances reflective thinking and ethical development in alignment with the MATATAG Curriculum.

Findings revealed a strong positive correlation between the frequency of student engagement with Penzu and improvements in reflective thinking, self-awareness, and value internalization among Grade 7 learners. Students who journaled more frequently demonstrated deeper ethical reasoning and richer personal insights, as supported by both quantitative results and qualitative interview data. Participants reported that Penzu offered a safe and engaging space that encouraged honesty, motivation, and meaningful reflection. The integration of AI-powered journaling strengthened the connection between classroom learning and real-life values, promoting ethical sensitivity and sustained engagement.

Overall, the study concludes that integrating AI-powered journaling tools like Penzu significantly enhances the depth and quality of student reflections in Values Education. By fostering consistent reflective practice and bridging academic content with lived experiences, such tools support self-awareness, ethical reasoning, and holistic development. It is recommended that schools consistently integrate AI journaling platforms aligned with curriculum goals, provide structured reflective prompts, and ensure teacher training in reflective pedagogy. Schools should also prioritize emotional safety, involve parents and school leaders, and implement continuous assessment strategies to strengthen values formation. Thoughtful integration of technology in Values Education can transform learning into a meaningful journey of moral growth and prepare students to navigate life’s complexities with integrity and empathy.

detail.abstract: This study employs open-source intelligence (OSINT) as its methodological framework to conduct a layered audit of two information chains within the 2005-2007 time window: "Hawking's participation in a scientific symposium in the U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI)" and "visits to private islands (including Little Saint James, LSJ)." The research centers on data assets D2-D8: D2 Evidence Ledger, D6 Claim Atoms, D7 Media Assets, and D8 Timeline Trunk. It replaces "subjective manual simulation coding" with deterministic algorithmic coding, quantifying reliability (consistency, Cohen's κ; robustness, correlation coefficient; anchor fact set consistency rate. Results indicate: A robust verifiable chain of facts can be constructed regarding "seminar attendance/conference activities"; however, "private island visits" currently appear in public materials as a chain dominated by secondary media and narrative amplification, exhibiting asymmetric evidence strength. This chain requires strict isolation from the factual chain to prevent slippage from "name mentions/photo narratives" to "illegal allegations." This report provides audit conclusions solely based on publicly verifiable materials and narrative contamination mechanisms. It makes no unproven inferences regarding motives nor unsubstantiated assertions about any criminal conduct.

detail.title: Sustainable Manufacturing Practices in Flexible Electronics Fabrication
detail.abstract: Flexible electronics are used in wearable devices, healthcare monitoring, energy harvesting, and smart packaging. Rapid advancements in these fields have also raised the concern of sustainability in the material used, fabrication processes, and end-of-life management. Flexible electronics systems are manufactured using processes that consume a great deal of energy, hazardous chemicals, and use non-biodegradable substrates, which contribute to the degradation of the environment and increase energy consumption. As production scales globally, these challenges are critical to resolve. This work reviews the sustainable options available for flexible electronics and integrates the studies on eco-friendly materials, less harmful manufacturing techniques, and design strategies. The work, in particular, examines the use of biodegradable and recyclable substrates, eco-friendly conductors, non-destructive fabrication techniques, and design for reuse and closed loops. The review also examines process strategies aimed at reducing the materials, water, and energy consumed. Recent literature assessing emerging patterns in resource and energy frugal manufacturing illustrates that eco-friendly manufacturing practices can yield comparable results to the traditional manufacturing processes with far less negative impact on the environment (Middha et al., 2024). The most significant takeaway remains that the practice of sustainably manufacturing flexible electronics is more than just an attainable goal; it is a practice that will serve to champion the developing needs of an expanding field and the accompanying policy frameworks. The integration of sustainability at the material, process, and system levels is critical for flexible electronics manufacturing (Kumar et al., 2024).

detail.abstract: Large-area printing technologies underpin the scalable manufacture of devices for energy, electronics, and photonic applications, yet their widespread industrial adoption remains constrained by materials inefficiency and cost instability. In particular, high-throughput processes frequently exhibit substantial material losses that undermine the economic advantages of printed manufacturing, motivating renewed attention to yield-and waste-aware process design (Pingale and Altay, 2025). This study adopts a comparative synthesis approach to evaluate dominant large-area deposition and patterning techniques, including roll-to-roll printing, inkjet printing, screen printing, and doctor-blade coating, alongside emerging hybrid manufacturing strategies that combine additive and continuous processes (Chen et al., 2023; Kant et al., 2023). By integrating reported process metrics, defect mechanisms, and cost models across these platforms, the analysis reveals that yield loss, solvent waste, and scale-dependent defects are the primary contributors to total manufacturing cost, outweighing the influence of raw material prices alone (Solanki et al., 2025; Rasool et al., 2023). Defect propagation over large areas and non-recoverable material losses during start-up, cleaning, and off-spec production emerge as critical economic bottlenecks. The findings underscore that sustainable cost reduction in large-area printed systems is not driven solely by material substitution, but by process-level materials control, defect mitigation, and design-for-manufacturing strategies that align material utilization with scalable production realities (Liu et al., 2024; Pathak et al., 2024).

title: Effects of Work-to-Family and Family-to-Work Enrichment on Staff Attitudes and Behaviors

detail.title: Effects of Work-to-Family and Family-to-Work Enrichment on Staff Attitudes and Behaviors
detail.abstract: This investigation tests the impact of work-to-family and family-to-work enrichment on job satisfaction and affective commitment. Also, it analyzes the impact of job satisfaction on affective commitment and the impact of job satisfaction and affective commitment on turnover intention. The investigation is based on a Spanish multisectoral sample of employed workers. The results confirmed all the model relationships except the impact of work-to-family enrichment on job satisfaction and affective commitment. Nor did they confirm the association between job satisfaction and turnover intention. Furthermore, managerial implications are derived to curb turnover intention through family-friendly policies that promote affective commitment and job satisfaction by means of work-family enrichment.

title: How to Avoid a Lack of Work Engagement among Public Police Professionals
affiliations: Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, Universidade de Santiago de Compostela - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration and University of Vigo

detail.title: How to Avoid a Lack of Work Engagement among Public Police Professionals
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the combined effect of five conditions-influence at work, interactional justice, workload, laissez-faire leadership, and emotional exhaustion-on the absence of work engagement in public police professionals. Using qualitative comparative analysis on a sample of 119 police professionals, the results show that none of the conditions on their own is necessary to lead to the absence of these professionals' work engagement. In addition, five casual configurations allow for the conclusion that influence at work, interactional justice, emotional exhaustion, and laissez-faire leadership are key conditions, while workload is less decisive in leading to the absence of work engagement in police professionals. The results inform managers of public police institutions on what variables can further contribute to creating workspaces in which learning, professional development, and positive experiences prevail among employees. This study is especially valuable to police professionals because the very nature of their work leads to engagement in acquiring a very powerful meaning.

detail.abstract: Contemporary approaches to AI safety and organisational reliability focus primarily on aligning intent, values, or objectives. However, many failures of intelligent systems arise not from misalignment or malice, but from the ability to act across incompatible operating contexts without explicit constraint. Unlike alignment and oversight approaches, this framework treats operating modes and commitment logic as primary design objects, specifying a minimal mode set and transition constraints that can be embedded directly into system architecture. This paper introduces the concept of mode-bounded intelligence: an architectural approach in which intelligent systems are constrained by explicit operating modes that govern authority, commitment formation, and reversibility of action. We argue that as system capability increases, discretion must decrease and procedure must increase — not as human bureaucracy, but as machine-enforced structural constraint. Modes are treated as properties of system state rather than agent identity, and are defined by their stance toward uncertainty, scope of authority, permissible commitments, and tolerance for failure. We formalise a minimal set of modes and specify design-level rules governing transitions between them. By treating commitments and authority as first-class system objects external to intelligence itself, mode-bounded systems prevent a common class of failure in which exploratory reasoning, operational execution, adjudication, and architectural change collapse into a single undifferentiated process. The result is a structural mitigation that scales with system capability, complements alignment-based approaches, and improves institutional coherence without relying on intent, values, or moral reasoning. This paper presents a design constraint rather than a normative doctrine, and delineates its scope and limitations accordingly.

title: Economic Impact of Yield Enhancement in Large-Scale Roll-to-Roll Printing
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Economic Impact of Yield Enhancement in Large-Scale Roll-to-Roll Printing
detail.abstract: Roll-to-roll (R2R) printing is a critical new manufacturing base paradigm when flexible electronic and energy devices are needed on scale, although its economics are heavily bound by the loss of yield due to defects, process variability, and wastage of materials. This paper explores the economics of an improvement in the yield of industrial R2R printing systems with special consideration of the reduction of waste and throughput stability, as well as the cost-effectiveness (Pingale and Altay 2025). The article makes use of evidence displaying case studies of industry, technology-economic investigations, and general literature on the manufacturing procedure to measure the change of yield advancements into quantifiable economic benefits in high-volume R2R applications such as printed electronics and energy appliances (Martin et al. 2022; Potoczny 2023). The analysis has shown that yields can be improved by a small percentage to result in disproportional cost of production and variability because the yield metrics are correlated with material utilization, effective speed of line, and cost per functional unit. The results also indicate that the benefits of scale are enhanced by yield improvement,t by stabilizing throughput as well as making production economics more predictable. The paper finds that the business of improving the yield should not be only considered as a technical optimization problem, but rather as a decisive economic instrument towards the attainment of scalable, competitive, and sustainable manufacturing systems, based on the R2R version (Abbel et al. 2014).

title: How to Moderate Emotional Exhaustion Among Public Healthcare Professionals?
affiliations: Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, Universidade de Santiago de Compostela - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration and University of Vigo

detail.title: How to Moderate Emotional Exhaustion Among Public Healthcare Professionals?
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the mediating role of employees' emotional exhaustion between laissez-faire leadership and employees' job attitudes (intrinsic satisfaction and turnover intention), and also the moderating role of influence at work, interactional justice and helping behaviors on employees' feelings of emotional exhaustion. Structural equation modeling and multigroup analysis were used in a sample of 511 public healthcare professionals. The results show that emotional exhaustion partially mediates the relationships between laissez-faire leadership and both intrinsic satisfaction and turnover intention. Influence at work moderates the relationship between laissez-faire leadership and emotional exhaustion; interactional justice moderates the relationship between emotional exhaustion and intrinsic satisfaction; and extra-role behaviors moderate the relationship between emotional exhaustion and turnover intention. To date, there are few studies analyzing the mediating role of emotional exhaustion in public healthcare, and there are no studies analyzing how its negative effects can be moderated. The conclusions may help human resources managers design new strategies to prevent and mitigate emotional exhaustion and contribute healthcare employees to cope with its serious effects, encouraging a healthy environment that gives priority to workers' well-being and service quality.

title: The Role of Graph Neural Networks in Operational Efficiency Across Industries
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Role of Graph Neural Networks in Operational Efficiency Across Industries
detail.abstract: This study examines the role of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in enhancing operational efficiency across multiple industries by enabling the modeling and analysis of complex relational data. As modern industrial systems increasingly rely on interconnected entities-such as suppliers, machines, patients, and infrastructure components-traditional machine learning approaches often struggle to capture their structural dependencies. This work adopts a structured synthesis methodology, systematically reviewing and integrating recent findings from both industrial implementations and peer-reviewed academic studies on GNN applications. The analysis highlights consistent performance gains achieved through GNN-based models, including improved prediction accuracy, optimized resource allocation, enhanced anomaly detection, and more effective decision-making processes. Empirical evidence across domains such as supply chain management, healthcare systems, smart manufacturing, and infrastructure networks demonstrates that GNNs outperform conventional models by leveraging topological and relational information inherent in operational data. The findings underscore the practical relevance of GNNs as a foundation for advanced operational intelligence. The study concludes by emphasizing the necessity of developing industry-specific adaptation frameworks to address domain constraints, scalability challenges, and interpretability requirements, thereby facilitating responsible and effective deployment of GNN-driven solutions in real-world operational environments (Bhat et al., 2025; Ahmed et al., 2025).

detail.abstract: Over the past century, organizational theory has consolidated fundamental concepts, structure, systems, authority, behavior, and culture, that explain how organizations function. These concepts remain valid and widely applied across academic literature and organizational practice. However, when examined through a chronological and systemic lens, they reveal a persistent structural gap: the absence of an explicit account of the human identity that precedes and sustains organizational coherence. This working paper proposes the Identity-Based Organization (IBO) not as a new management model, but as a foundational requirement that becomes evident once the organizational field is conceptually organized. Identity is presented as the originating condition that allows structures, systems, and cultures to operate with legitimacy, continuity, and internal coherence over time. By making identity explicit as the antecedent of organizational culture and behavior, this paper offers a theoretical response to recurring phenomena such as fragmentation, superficial alignment, and resistance to cultural initiatives. The Identity-Based Organization does not replace existing organizational concepts; rather, it organizes and potentiates them, providing the conceptual substrate necessary for their full and responsible application.

title: Impact of Post-Tipping Policy on Online Delivery Platform
affiliations: Independent, Oklahoma State University - Management Science and Information Systems and Baylor University - Hankamer School of Business

detail.title: Impact of Post-Tipping Policy on Online Delivery Platform
detail.abstract: The platform economy faces persistent challenges in designing incentive mechanisms that effectively align gig worker motivation with service quality and customer satisfaction. Following New York City's minimum wage regulations for app-based delivery workers, DoorDash implemented a post-tipping policy in December 2023. Previously, customers could tip before placing the order (pre-tipping). Under the new policy, customers can tip only after the order is delivered (post-tipping). This study examines the behavioral and operational implications of this policy change, focusing on order volume and tipping behavior. Methodology/Results: Combining game-theoretic modeling with econometric analysis, we find that the post-tipping policy has negative impacts on both order volume and tipping behavior, while introducing delivery effort uncertainties due to the diminished upfront incentives for Dashers. These findings underscore the critical role of information asymmetry, particularly the lack of pre-service tip visibility, in shaping stakeholder decisions. Managerial Implications: Our results contribute to the literature on platform operations and gig economy incentive design by demonstrating how policy-driven shifts in incentive timing can disrupt the delicate balance between customer expectations, worker motivation, and platform profitability. This study also offers actionable insights for platforms navigating regulatory pressures while optimizing incentive structures to sustain service quality and user engagement.

title: Employment Gap in Egypt: Hidden Causes and Necessary Solutions

detail.title: Employment Gap in Egypt: Hidden Causes and Necessary Solutions
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the main challenges facing the employment process in Egypt, focusing on labor supply and demand, the mismatch between education and market needs, workplace issues, bureaucracy, and the lack of youth skills. The study relies on reviewing local and international literature and reports, as well as analyzing the current state of the Egyptian labor market. The study concludes that addressing employment challenges requires developing the technical education system, expanding vocational training, activating digital transformation in recruitment, and encouraging the private sector to create decent and sustainable jobs.
